turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Jess? Come on through, the doctor's free. I'll put your vitals up in a moment.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Howzit Jess. Your partner can sit by the window. What's actually been bothering you, in your own words?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ag, shame, it's nothing serious. My heart just flutters a bit. He made the appointment, I would've left it.
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She keeps saying nothing. I've seen her bolt upright at two in the morning, breathing like she sprinted, hand flat on her chest.
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay, ja, I wake up and it's going fast. It's not... I'm not gasping. I'm alright after a minute, truly.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fast like a pounding, or skipping beats, or just speedy?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Speedy, a flutter in the chest, mostly at night and also right before an exam or a work meeting. And before you say it, I'm not stressed, I don't do stress.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Noted, you don't call it stress. Is the short breath right there with the fast heart?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, with it. I get puffed, that's all, not like I can't get air in. Mostly those same times, night and before I have to perform.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain, actual pain, when it happens?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No, no pain. Never had pain.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): And have you blacked out, or felt you were about to?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No ways. I stay awake, I'm fine.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): When did it start? Even a rough season is useful.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Um, last winter, or the one before. I honestly can't date it, it wasn't after a specific weekend, it just was there.
[SEG0016] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I've tried to think as well. I can't put a month on it either.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll leave the start date open. Coffee, energy drinks, how much in a day?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, four cups, maybe five. And a Monster if there's a deadline. It's not hectic.
[SEG0019] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's a Monster in the car and another at her desk, and the vape is in her hand the whole time.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine, two Monsters, sometimes three if varsity and work land on the same day. The vape is just mint. I switched off cigarettes ages ago, so that's sorted.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nicotine is still nicotine, hey. Any tablets a doctor has you on, even something now and then?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I don't take medicine, nothing regular and nothing occasional.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Allergies to medicines, foods, anything that swells you up or brings a rash?
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergies. Never had one.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Asthma, a thyroid problem, any heart condition you've been told about?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No, none of that. I've always just cracked on.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, random, but the N1 was a proper mess this morning. We sat through three cycles at that robot by Canal Walk.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): And then he wanted to talk about the Proteas the whole way. Did you see that catch at the boundary? The third umpire bottled it completely.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ja, I saw the highlights with my coffee. That lbw was a shocker. Wind was mad yesterday as well, dust everywhere.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): My brother's little boy tried to fly a kite in it. Thing went straight over the neighbour's wall and we spent ages fetching it out of a lemon tree.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): He's four and already shouting at the TV umpire. Lekker attitude. Anyway, sorry, we got sidetracked.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sharp, no problem. Let me examine you, then Sister can read me those numbers.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lungs are clear both sides, no wheeze. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. Pulse is regular, just a bit quick. Ankles aren't swollen.
[SEG0034] person_1 (NURSE): On the monitor just now: blood pressure one twenty eight over seventy eight, pulse one hundred and four, sats ninety eight percent, respiratory rate eighteen.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): So I'm thinking out loud. The flutter and the puffing, clustered at night and before you have to perform, plus that much caffeine and the vape, that package often is the stimulant load. I still don't want to miss an overactive thyroid or a rhythm problem.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): So you think it's just the coffee. I can live with that. I don't need a whole workup.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think that's the likely story, but it's not proven, and I'm not happy to stop there. I'd like an ECG today, and thyroid bloods, TSH and free T4.
[SEG0038] person_1 (NURSE): ECG bay is open. I can do the tracing when you finish, and the lab downstairs will take the bloods.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): An ECG is a bit much for a flutter, but ja, fine, if you say so.

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): While we wait on those, when it starts, try a slow breath: in for four counts, hold for four, out for six. Do a few rounds at night and before a meeting. And cut the Monsters and the extra coffee, and ease off the vape if you can.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll hide the Monsters. She won't.
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Ag, I'll try. I'm not promising I'll become a herbal tea person.
[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Come back in two weeks and we'll go through the ECG and the bloods. If you get actual chest pain, or you faint, don't wait, come straight in or to casualty.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Two weeks is fine. It won't be anything.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): Sharp, I'll walk you to the ECG after this. Lab forms I'll print just now.

spec.situation: Young adult with palpitations and breathlessness, worse at night and before exams or work meetings; downplays stress, drinks a lot of coffee and energy drinks, vapes; friend or partner contributes. Doctor orders ECG and thyroid tests, discusses breathing exercises.
features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

bad.reason: Current vaping and partner detail supported; nicotine is doctor-stated, not patient-reported.
bad.text: smoking (description=Vapes mint-flavoured nicotine through the day, status=current, details=Partner reports the vape is in her hand the whole time, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: She says 'I'm not stressed'; this doesn't clearly establish stress as absent clinically.

omissions.text: Shortness of breath was specifically qualified as 'puffed' and 'not like I can't get air in' / 'not gasping'; this denied severe dyspnoea during episodes.

There is a real disagreement/minimisation: patient says it is 'nothing serious' and would have left it, while partner reports nocturnal episodes with sitting bolt upright, breathing hard, and hand on chest; patient also says she does not want 'a whole workup' and feels ECG is 'a bit much', whereas doctor says further workup is still needed.
No current medicines at all: patient denied both regular and occasional tablets/medicines.

Doctor advised the breathing exercise specifically as a few rounds when symptoms start, at night and before a meeting; recorded plan says 'before meetings' but omits the singular 'before a meeting' wording is minor, however the instruction to do a few rounds is missing.
Follow-up purpose was to review both the ECG and the blood tests in two weeks.

Breathlessness is described as mild: she gets puffed/short of breath with the fast heart but is not gasping and not unable to get air in.
No food or medication allergies causing swelling or rash were reported; the allergy question explicitly included medicines, foods, swelling and rash.
Nicotine use from vaping was explicitly discussed by the doctor ('Nicotine is still nicotine'), not just mint flavour vaping.
